title: Pet Turf and Dog Runs in Johnstown, CO | NoCo Turf Co.
description: Johnstown's code makes a dog area whose odor or drainage offends the neighbors a public nuisance. Plus its four-animal cap, leash rule and HOA dog-run reviews.
h1: In Johnstown, a dog run whose odor or drainage offends the neighbors is a public nuisance.
lede: Johnstown rewrote its nuisance-animal rules in November 2023, and the rewritten section judges the place a dog is kept by what reaches the neighbors: odor, dust, noise and drainage. On a turf run, drainage is the part that gets built.

answer.question: What does Johnstown's code say about a backyard dog run?
answer.answer: Sec. 7-135(c) requires any area where animals are kept to be maintained without odors, dust, noise or drainage offensive to adjoining properties, and a code enforcement or police officer can make a prima facie call on it. The Town also limits residents to four animals, birds included. NoCo Turf Co. installs dog runs and pet turf in Johnstown, Colorado.

blocks.h2: Odor, dust, noise and drainage are judged from the neighbor's side of the fence.
blocks.takeaway: Ordinance 2023-255 made the condition of the place an animal is kept, not only the animal's behavior, a public nuisance.
paras: The Town Council passed Ordinance 2023-255 on its November 20, 2023 consent agenda, rewriting Sec. 7-135. Subsection (c) says areas where animals are kept must be maintained so they create no odors, dust, noise or drainage offensive to the use or enjoyment of adjoining properties, as reasonable people of ordinary sensibilities would judge it. A code enforcement officer, police officer or other designated officer may make a prima facie determination, and failing to keep the area that way is a public nuisance.

The section still lists an animal at large and persistent barking or howling as nuisances, and Sec. 7-136 makes a dog left in a yard to bark excessively or continuously its own offense. On a turf run, subsection (c) is the clause the build answers: urine has to go down through the base and stay on your lot instead of running across the surface toward the fence line. The [pet turf page](/services/pet-turf/) covers the layers.

blocks.h2: Four animals, birds included, and a leash no longer than 10 feet.
paras: The Town's animal-control answers set a limit of four animals, birds included. Every animal except a domestic cat must be under its owner's control, and a dog must be on a leash 10 feet long or shorter, attached to the dog or held or tied by a person.

Every dog and cat needs a Town license bought each year, good from May 1 to April 30, and every dog and cat six months or older needs a rabies vaccination. The code defines at large as off the owner's premises and not under the owner's control, so a dog that slips through a gap at the edge of a run is at large the moment it leaves the lot.

blocks.h2: Thompson Crossing and Mountain View West review dog runs, and one guide still lists synthetic turf as barred.
paras: Thompson Crossing's design guidelines, created in 2005 and revised in 2006, put the materials, colors and location of dog houses and dog runs up for design review committee approval, and bar any change to a lot's drainage pattern that harms the lots next door. The phase 2 guide, revised April 21, 2014, repeats the dog-run rule. Mountain View West, the downtown mixed-use PUD, allows dog runs, dog houses, playhouses and swing sets only with special use approval.

Both Thompson Crossing guides also list synthetic turf among items not permitted under any circumstances. They predate Colorado's backyard turf protections, shown below; the committee's review of the run itself, its location and its drainage still applies.

blocks.h2: The dog park in the Town's plans is a shaded 0.75 acre by the Little Thompson River.
paras: The parks master plan the Town posts for its 61-acre park site half a mile south of downtown, at Parish Avenue on the Little Thompson River, draws a 0.75-acre shaded dog park with active and inactive dog areas in the park's northeast corner. Dog parks were among the most common requests in the plan's public survey, and the Town says Council approved that park's master plan in 2026.
The 2023 code rewrite also lets any leashed dog into a Town park, according to the staff memo the Town Attorney presented with the ordinance.

faq.q: Where does a dog found at large in Johnstown end up?
faq.a: At NOCO Humane's Larimer Campus in Loveland, where it's scanned for a microchip and held 5 days. The shelter sets its own fees for holding and vet care, and those don't include any Town fine or court costs.

faq.q: Who takes a barking complaint in Johnstown?
faq.a: Johnstown Police. The Town's animal-control FAQ says the animal code gives the police the power to enforce the barking rule, and it lists the non-emergency line for reports.

faq.q: Do cats follow the same rules in Johnstown?
faq.a: They need the same yearly license and rabies vaccination. With those, the Town lets cats roam, and officers won't pick up a healthy stray cat that wanders onto your property.
